sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-editor-2026-10-02-r3/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx — Quality Checks!A3:D3 and Internal Quality Checks!A3:D3; both define row 2 as preserving an authentic, casual/terse human voice and avoiding robotic or over-polished prose; the internal sheet adds no row-specific annotation
evidence: Workbook row Quality Checks!A3:D3 asks for authentic casual/terse prose rather than robotic, over-polished copy; the mirrored Internal Quality Checks row has no additional annotation. The frozen instruction meets that bar. instruction.md:1 opens in first person with the contraction "I'd" and a concrete personal workflow ("I often paste a long one-line experiment..."), then varies its cadence with the short direct request at line 3 and the plain delivery sentence at line 5. It has no marketing gloss, slogan language, acceptance-list scaffolding, or perfectly parallel bullets. The six notes keep the same practical voice while becoming appropriately more direct: overview.md:1 uses the terse heading "The playground"; overview.md:3-5 describes the editor in ordinary product terms; policy.md:1 is the conversational heading "Choices left to you"; policy.md:3-5 explicitly leaves layout, labels, routes, schema, wording, and examples flexible. The denser technical notes still use varied sentences and concrete verbs rather than uniform boilerplate (for example behaviour.md:3-7 and ui.md:3-17). A plausible broken app, such as a static mock, could still pass this instruction-only voice row, so app quality is not mistaken for evidence here. Conversely, a conforming app paired with a robotic, uniformly parallel brief could fail this row; the current brief does not have that wording defect. Manifest hashes bind instruction.md to 4848dc698fbbe6f4bf88816f9119893424cd7d59c6d595f6ebf1ed7c0d91ac33 and the workbook to 6d44970b2ff67fefad1e2327e743fc226fcd4c50ff55baf899f41069a9b3fd7f, matching the files inspected.
